failure_reason: Direct HTTP fetch worked for the whole session (no WAF/DataDome/CAPTCHA on any real content page fetched). Mid-investigation, repeated speculative /shop/best-sellers/<dept-slug> and /shop/<dept>/new-arrivals probes began returning a Walmart soft anti-scan redirect (HTTP 307 -> /blocked?url=...) for BOTH new guesses AND a previously-successful URL re-fetched later, while /cp/ hub pages kept returning 200 throughout. This looks like a path-class rate/pattern trigger on /shop/*, not a full host block (Rule: 'the FIRST block stops that host' - treated conservatively as stop-probing-this-path-family). All data below was captured before that trigger. Departments not yet checked via a direct URL probe for a dedicated Best Sellers page: Appliances, Mattresses, Luggage, Kids' Rooms (not fetched at all), and Bath/Bedding/Kitchen & Dining/Patio & Garden (their /cp/ hub pages were fetched and scanned for a 'Best Sellers' nav/hubspoke link - zero found on any of the four - but the /shop/best-sellers/<slug> URL pattern itself was only positively confirmed to exist for one slug ('storage-and-organization') and positively confirmed NOT to exist for 'decor' and 'furniture' (real in-site 404 'Uh-oh...' page, itemCount 0, not a block) before the block hit; bath/bedding/kitchen-and-dining/patio-and-garden slugs were not reached before the block began.
notes: SCOPE: task brief scopes this company to Home + Furniture + Patio & Garden (home-adjacent) + Home Decor, not Walmart's whole store, so I treated Walmart's own 'Home' department (cat_id 4044, which internally contains Décor, Furniture, Bath, Bedding, Kitchen & Dining, Storage & Organization, Appliances, Mattresses, Luggage, Kids' Rooms) plus the separate Patio & Garden department (cat_id 5428) as in-scope. NAVIGATION DISCOVERY: fetched and inspected (1) the Home dept mega-menu on /cp/home/4044 (all 15 top-level nav categories and their subcategory link lists), (2) the Décor hub /cp/decor/133012 ('Currently Trending' hubspoke module), (3) the Furniture hub /cp/furniture/103150 ('More to explore' hubspoke module), (4) the Storage & Organization hub /cp/storage-organization/90828 ('More to explore' hubspoke module), (5) Bath hub /cp/bath/539095, (6) Bedding hub /cp/bedding/539103, (7) Kitchen & Dining hub /cp/kitchen-dining/623679, (8) Patio & Garden hub /cp/patio-garden/5428. Did not use robots.txt-disallowed /search (site's own search is off-limits per robots.txt: 'Disallow: /search'); relied on mega-menu + hub-page hubspoke modules + sitemap-adjacent nav instead, per brief's own priority order. FINDING: Only Storage & Organization exposes a genuine, site-labelled 'Best sellers' PLP (hubspoke pill literally named 'Best sellers' on its own hub page, distinct from the ubiquitous per-product 'Best seller' badge that appears on ~30-280 individual product tiles on nearly every Home page - those badges were excluded per brief section 3 rule 3, they do not make a PDP/tile a Bestsellers PLP). Décor and Furniture hub pages carry ZERO 'Best Sellers'/'Bestsellers' nav mentions (only per-product badges), and direct URL probes /shop/best-sellers/decor and /shop/best-sellers/furniture both resolved to Walmart's own real 'Uh-oh...' not-found page (totalItemCount 0, a genuine site 404, not a block) - this is real absence evidence for those two, not just an unexplored gap. Bath/Bedding/Kitchen & Dining/Patio & Garden hub pages also show zero 'Best Sellers' nav mentions, but the URL-pattern probe for those specific slugs was cut short by the /shop/ path block, so absence there is probable but not proven to the same standard - hence 'partial' rather than 'ok'.
